audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this an EVEN matchup at 6/10 while the win rate is 43.51% over 154 games and the level chart gives Gragas 4 of 7 stages with Trundle winning none. The content layer already contradicts it in prose ('Respect the 40% win rate').
audit.why: 43.51% is a losing lane, not an even one, and the two layers must not disagree about difficulty.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN to HARD, tone to the hard colour, diffRating and the difficulty/rating lines to 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes are listed with no cooldown attached to the one that decides the lane. Body Slam is called 'his escape' four times without a duration.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s and Explosive Cask is 100/85/70s. The whole punish window is 'he used Body Slam, you have 14 seconds' — without the number the advice is unusable.
audit.corrected: Added the 14s Body Slam window and the 100s Cask cooldown to early, mid, late and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) Gragas is repeatedly credited with 'passive stacking' and a 'passive health bar' — he has neither; his passive is Happy Hour, which heals on ability use. (b) Damage reduction is attributed to 'his W's passive Drunken Rage' — Drunken Rage is a 5s active, not a passive. (c) The text twice claims he can 'Body Slam through your Pillar terrain', which inverts the single most important interaction in the matchup.
audit.why: Riot text: Happy Hour — 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill'. Drunken Rage — 'Gragas samples his latest brew for 1 second. After finishing... reducing damage received.' Pillar of Ice — 'becoming impassable terrain'; Body Slam — 'Gragas charges to a location'. A ground dash into impassable terrain stops on it.
audit.corrected: Named Happy Hour (P) and Drunken Rage (W) correctly, flagged the 1-second drink animation as the burst tell, and reversed the Pillar claim: Pillar of Ice walls Body Slam off.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling as a first back is already listed and is the right call — Happy Hour plus Barrel Roll sustain is what wins him extended poke wars, and Frozen Domain amplifies healing on your side too, so Grievous Wounds on you costs double.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Dodge his E body slam' teaches the wrong reflex — sidestepping a targeted-location dash is unreliable.
audit.why: Pillar of Ice denies the dash outright; dodging is the fallback, not the plan.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].t changed to Pillar his E body slam.

edits.before: At level 1 you both have one ability and neither has a real edge — Q Chomp trades are fine but Gragas's Barrel Roll splashes and begins stacking his passive health bar immediately. Hold your ground but don't over-commit. The real problem starts at level 2: Gragas gets Body Slam and now has a dash you cannot reliably block with Pillar because you don't have it yet. He will Body Slam in, auto, and dash back out of any trade you try to extend — that mobility eats your pattern alive at this stage.
edits.after: At level 1 you both have one ability and neither has a real edge — Q Chomp trades are fine, but Barrel Roll splashes and every cast he makes triggers Happy Hour (P) to heal him back. Hold your ground but don't over-commit. The real problem starts at level 2: Gragas gets Body Slam on a 14s cooldown and has a dash you cannot wall off with Pillar because you don't have it yet. He will Body Slam in, auto, and dash back out of any trade you try to extend — that mobility eats your pattern alive.

edits.before: Neither has a movement tool at level 1 — Chomp bite trades are roughly even against Gragas's Barrel Roll splash and passive stacking.
edits.after: Neither has a movement tool at level 1 — Chomp bite trades are roughly even against Barrel Roll splash and the Happy Hour heal each cast refunds.

edits.before: Gragas's Drunken Rage passive and Q sustain compound with his item scaling; he out-paces your King's Tribute regen in extended poke wars and you cannot force him to fight on your terms.
edits.after: Drunken Rage (W) is a 5s active that cuts the damage he takes right before he swings, and Happy Hour heals off every cast, so he out-paces King's Tribute in any extended poke war.

edits.before: Level 3 is your one realistic window — drop Frozen Domain before he can Body Slam away, Pillar behind him to cut off the dash route, and bite his AD with Chomp while you chase on the W movement speed. If he wastes Body Slam to initiate rather than escape, you can cash the pattern. But from levels 4-6 Gragas wins decisively: his W's passive Drunken Rage grants damage reduction right before any trade, his Q sustain out-paces your King's Tribute in a poke war, and at 6 Explosive Cask ends any fight on his terms by knocking you clean off Frozen Domain and stripping every W bonus you built up. Do not hard commit to an all-in from 5 onward without a guaranteed Pillar placement.
edits.after: Level 3 is your one realistic window — drop Frozen Domain before he can Body Slam away, then put Pillar of Ice in his dash lane, because Body Slam is a ground charge and impassable terrain stops it dead. Bite his AD with Chomp while you chase on the W movement speed. If he burns Body Slam to initiate, you own the next 14 seconds. From levels 4-6 Gragas wins decisively: Drunken Rage (W) is a 5s active cutting incoming damage right before he swings, Happy Hour heals him off every cast, and at 6 Explosive Cask knocks you clean off Frozen Domain and strips every W bonus you built up. Do not commit an all-in from 5 onward without Pillar placed first.

edits.before: Gragas with a first item out-sustains and out-displaces you — he can Body Slam through your Pillar terrain if he reads it, tank inside your W with Drunken Rage reduction, and R-knockback you out of Frozen Domain the moment you pop Subjugate. Your only win condition late is catching him without Body Slam and opening R immediately so the armor drain compounds over the full fight; but Gragas can simply rotate away or call in his team. Respect the 40% win rate, play for objective contests where Subjugate hitting a tanky frontliner matters more than winning the Gragas 1v1 directly.
edits.after: Gragas with a first item out-sustains and out-displaces you — he tanks inside your W behind Drunken Rage's damage cut and R-knocks you out of Frozen Domain the second you pop Subjugate. Pillar of Ice still walls Body Slam off, so the dash is not what saves him; the 100-second Explosive Cask is. Your win condition late is catching him with Cask down and opening R immediately so the resist drain compounds over the full fight. Respect the 43% win rate: play objective contests where Subjugate on their biggest frontliner matters more than the Gragas 1v1.

edits.before: Gragas rushes Sunfire or Heartsteel and becomes a sustained brawler who can Body Slam through your Pillar and trade back inside your own W zone.
edits.after: Gragas rushes Sunfire or Heartsteel and becomes a brawler who can tank your W zone — but Pillar of Ice is terrain and still stops Body Slam cold.

edits.after: Put Pillar of Ice in his Body Slam lane — it is impassable terrain and stops the charge dead

edits.after: Overall difficulty: 7/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Body Slam and how disciplined your pattern is.
